title: Telemetry: tag requests with rollout_id + cohort for Hosted canary comparisons (cardinality-safe)
author: Caleb Johnson
release_notes: Adds cohort tagging (baseline/canary) and rollout-aware aggregation hooks to enable baseline vs canary metric comparisons in Console.
Rollout ID is propagated through request context and traces/logs, but is not emitted as a default label on core request metrics to avoid cardinality blowups.
Introduces an allowlisted, TTL-bounded rollouts metrics namespace keyed by rollout_id for active rollouts only.
description:
## Context
Hosted canary rollouts need baseline vs canary comparisons for key SLO signals (5xx, timeouts, p95 latency) and throughput/cost signals (tokens/sec, in/out token counts). The routing/data plane work (ENG-9123) can split traffic, but without consistent request tagging we can’t build accurate cohort dashboards or auto-stop conditions.

A hard constraint here is metrics cardinality: emitting `rollout_id` on all request metrics will explode series count and degrade dashboards/alerting, especially on high-QPS tenants.

This PR implements request tagging and aggregation hooks that make cohort comparison possible while keeping the default metrics surface cardinality-safe.

## What’s included
1) Request context tagging
- Adds `rollout_id` (string) and `rollout_cohort` (enum: `baseline|canary|none`) to the shared request context.
- Tags are set by the router when a rollout split is applied (baseline path and canary path).
- Propagates tags through:
  - gateway -> data plane request context
  - internal tracing attributes
  - structured request logs

2) Metrics strategy (cardinality-safe)
- Core request metrics keep their existing low-cardinality label set (route, region, status class, etc.).
- We emit `rollout_cohort` as a label ONLY on a small, explicitly scoped set of “rollout cohort” metrics (new namespace), not on the global request metrics.
- `rollout_id` is NOT emitted as a label on the global request metrics.
- Instead, `rollout_id` is:
  - attached to traces/logs (for debugging)
  - used by a rollouts-specific aggregation path that is allowlisted + TTL bounded

3) Rollouts metrics aggregation hooks
- Introduces a rollouts-only metrics namespace where `rollout_id` is an allowed dimension, but only for rollouts in an “active allowlist”.
- Adds an in-process allowlist cache keyed by `rollout_id` with TTL refresh from control plane (default 5 minutes). If the allowlist entry expires, we stop emitting the rollout_id series.
- Metrics emitted under this namespace include:
  - `rollouts.requests_total{rollout_id, cohort, route, region}`
  - `rollouts.errors_total{rollout_id, cohort, route, region, error_class}`
  - `rollouts.latency_ms_bucket{rollout_id, cohort, route, region}` (histogram)
  - `rollouts.timeouts_total{rollout_id, cohort, route, region}`
  - `rollouts.tokens_in_total` / `rollouts.tokens_out_total` (where available)

4) Naming / schema notes
- Uses the prefix `rollouts.*` for the new metrics namespace.
- Tracing attributes use `rw.rollout.id` and `rw.rollout.cohort`.
- Log fields use `rollout_id` and `rollout_cohort` (matching existing structured log conventions).

## Why this approach
- `cohort` is low cardinality and safe to use broadly, but even cohort + route + region is still manageable only if we scope where it’s emitted.
- `rollout_id` is inherently high cardinality. Restricting it to an allowlisted metrics namespace ensures:
  - dashboards/alerts can query per-rollout during the soak window
  - series disappear after the rollout is complete (or after TTL), preventing long-tail series buildup
  - we can set explicit budgets and instrumentation ownership for this feature

## Implementation details
- Router sets tags using the existing rollout evaluation result (from the split primitive) and injects into `RequestContext`.
- Telemetry layer reads from `RequestContext` and:
  - always attaches tags to tracing span attributes
  - always attaches tags to structured logs
  - conditionally emits rollouts metrics when `rollout_id` is present AND allowlisted
- Allowlist provider (control plane) is called on cache miss and periodically refreshed; errors fall back to “not allowlisted” to protect metrics systems.

## Tests
- Unit tests:
  - RequestContext serialization/deserialization includes rollout tags.
  - Allowlist TTL behavior (refresh, expire -> stop emitting).
  - Metrics emission only under allowlisted conditions.
- Integration-ish test (mocked allowlist):
  - baseline vs canary requests increment separate `rollouts.*` series.

## Operational notes / limitations
- If control plane is degraded, we bias toward NOT emitting rollout_id metrics (still keep trace/log tags).
- For streaming retries: tags stay stable across internal retries because cohort assignment happens before request execution and is copied into context; we don’t re-roll cohort on retry.
- This PR does not add dashboards; it only provides the tagging + metric hooks. Dashboards/alerts are tracked in follow-ups (ENG-9152 and PR-28910).

## Follow-ups
- Wire allowlist membership to orchestrator state transitions (start/stop rollout) so series appear/disappear deterministically (tracked under ENG-9152).
- Add explicit cardinality budgeting + alerts for rollouts namespace (tracked under ENG-9152).

- Aisha Bello: Requested consistent naming across logs/traces/metrics and to ensure timeouts are broken out for stop-conditions work. Added `timeouts_total` and aligned attribute names.
- Mina Haddad: Confirmed cohort stickiness behavior for retries/streaming. Added notes and ensured context copy is stable across retries.
